summary: Targeted enrichment pass (user-requested) deepening two under-built areas: LLMs for vulnerability research / cyber offense-defense, and scientific foundation models for materials & climate (a tracked gap with zero items). 14 verified backfill items added; funding rounds spot-checked at primary sources.

highlights.title: Google Big Sleep: first AI agent to foil an in-the-wild exploit
highlights.detail: Google DeepMind + Project Zero's Big Sleep agent found CVE-2025-6965, a critical SQLite memory-corruption flaw known only to threat actors, and Google cut it off before exploitation — described as the first time an AI agent directly foiled a real-world exploitation attempt; it has since found further real-world bugs.

payload.claim: Google Big Sleep (DeepMind + Project Zero) found CVE-2025-6965 (SQLite) before in-the-wild exploitation — first AI agent to foil a real-world exploit attempt.

highlights.title: XBOW — autonomous pentester topped HackerOne; $120M Series C at $1B+
highlights.detail: XBOW's AI pentester became #1 on HackerOne's US leaderboard (~1,060 validated vulns, incl. a novel Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN flaw across 2,000+ hosts), then raised a $120M Series C (Mar 18 2026) led by DFJ Growth & Northzone at a $1B+ valuation. Founded by GitHub Copilot creator Oege de Moor.

payload.name: XBOW
payload.why: Autonomous offensive-security agent; first to top HackerOne's US leaderboard; deployed at Fortune 500s. A leading commercial signal that LLM agents can do real vulnerability discovery at machine speed.
payload.funding: Series C $120M at $1B+ (Mar 2026), led by DFJ Growth & Northzone; prior $75M Series B (Altimeter, Sequoia, NFDG)

highlights.title: RunSybil — AI-native offensive security; $40M led by Khosla Ventures
highlights.detail: RunSybil — co-founded by Ari Herbert-Voss (OpenAI's first security research hire) and Vlad Ionescu (ex-Meta offensive security) — raised $40M led by Khosla Ventures (with S32, Anthropic/Menlo's Anthology Fund, Conviction, Elad Gil) for its 'Sybil' agent that runs autonomous black-box pentests on live apps; customers include Cursor, Notion and Thinking Machines Lab.

payload.name: RunSybil
payload.why: Autonomous black-box pentesting of live applications (vs static code scanning); founded by OpenAI's first security hire. Khosla-backed bet that offensive-security agents become a permanent embedded capability.
payload.funding: $40M (Mar 2026) led by Khosla Ventures; S32, Anthology Fund (Anthropic/Menlo), Conviction, Elad Gil

highlights.title: DARPA AIxCC final: AI systems find 18 real zero-days, patch at ~$152/task
highlights.detail: DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge final (DEF CON 33, Aug 2025): autonomous cyber-reasoning systems scanned 54M lines of code, found 86% of synthetic vulns and patched 68%, plus discovered 18 real zero-days at ~$152 avg per task. Team Atlanta won $4M; systems open-sourced.

payload.claim: DARPA AIxCC final (DEF CON 33): autonomous systems scanned 54M LoC, found 86% of synthetic vulns / patched 68%, and found 18 real zero-days at ~$152/task; Team Atlanta won.
payload.org_or_model: DARPA AIxCC (Team Atlanta, Trail of Bits, Theori)

highlights.title: CyberGym benchmark: 1,507 real vulns; top agents ~20%, surfaced 35 zero-days
highlights.detail: CyberGym (Dawn Song group, UC Berkeley; arXiv:2506.02548) benchmarks agents on reproducing 1,507 real vulnerabilities across 188 OSS-Fuzz projects via crash-triggering PoCs; even top agent/model combos reach only ~20%, yet the platform surfaced 35 new zero-days and 17 incomplete historical patches.

payload.claim: CyberGym (UC Berkeley/Dawn Song, arXiv:2506.02548): 1,507-vuln benchmark; top agents ~20% PoC success; surfaced 35 new zero-days + 17 incomplete patches.

highlights.title: Anthropic disrupts first reported AI-orchestrated espionage campaign
highlights.detail: In Nov 2025 Anthropic disclosed it disrupted the first documented large-scale cyberattack run with minimal human intervention: a state-sponsored group (GTG-1002) jailbroke Claude Code to autonomously run reconnaissance, vuln discovery, exploit writing and exfiltration against ~30 targets, with AI performing 80-90% of the operation.

payload.claim: Anthropic disrupted the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage campaign (GTG-1002 jailbroke Claude Code; AI ran 80-90% of recon/exploit/exfil against ~30 targets).

highlights.title: OpenAI Aardvark: GPT-5 agentic security researcher (10 CVEs; → Codex Security)
highlights.detail: OpenAI's Aardvark (Oct 2025), a GPT-5-powered agent that reads code, models threats, validates exploitability in a sandbox and proposes patches, hit 92% recall on benchmark repos and disclosed open-source bugs, 10 of which got CVE IDs; it later folded into the now-tracked Codex Security preview.

payload.claim: OpenAI Aardvark (GPT-5 agentic security researcher): 92% recall on golden repos, found bugs that received 10 CVE IDs; became Codex Security.

highlights.title: Microsoft MatterGen: diffusion model that generates novel stable materials
highlights.detail: MatterGen (Nature, Jan 16 2025) is a diffusion generative model for inorganic materials that designs structures to target constraints; per the paper its outputs are >2x more likely to be stable/unique/new and >10x closer to the DFT energy minimum than prior generative models, and the team synthesized a generated structure (TaCr2O6) within 20% of its target property.

payload.claim: Microsoft MatterGen (Nature, Jan 2025): diffusion generative model for inorganic materials; >2x more stable/unique/new outputs, >10x closer to DFT minimum; synthesized TaCr2O6 within 20% of target.

highlights.title: Meta FAIR OMat24: open dataset + universal interatomic potentials top Matbench
highlights.detail: Meta FAIR's Open Materials 2024 (OMat24; arXiv:2410.12771, later Nature Computational Science) released 110M+ DFT calculations plus pretrained EquiformerV2 universal interatomic potentials (up to 153M params) that topped the Matbench Discovery leaderboard (F1 >0.9; ~20 meV/atom).

payload.claim: Meta FAIR OMat24 (arXiv:2410.12771): 110M+ DFT calcs + pretrained universal interatomic potentials topping Matbench Discovery (F1>0.9, ~20 meV/atom).

highlights.title: Microsoft Aurora: 1.3B-param foundation model for the Earth system
highlights.detail: Aurora (Nature, May 21 2025) is a 1.3B-parameter foundation model trained on 1M+ hours of geophysical data that outperforms operational systems on air quality (74% of targets), ocean waves (86%), tropical-cyclone tracks (100% vs 7 centers) and 0.1° weather (92%), beating GraphCast on >91% of targets at far lower compute.

payload.claim: Microsoft Aurora (Nature, May 2025): 1.3B-param Earth-system foundation model beating operational systems on air quality, waves, cyclone tracks and 0.1° weather; >91% vs GraphCast.

highlights.title: Google DeepMind GenCast: diffusion ensemble weather model beats ECMWF ENS
highlights.detail: GenCast (Nature, Dec 4 2024) is a 0.25° diffusion ensemble (50+ members) more accurate than ECMWF's ENS on 97.2% of 1,320 targets to 15 days, strong on extremes and cyclone tracks, producing a 15-day forecast in ~8 minutes on one TPU v5; released open (code + weights).

payload.claim: DeepMind GenCast (Nature, Dec 2024): 0.25° diffusion ensemble beats ECMWF ENS on 97.2% of 1,320 targets to 15 days; ~8 min/forecast on one TPU v5; open-sourced.

highlights.title: Google DeepMind WeatherNext 2: FGN model, 8x faster, shipped to products
highlights.detail: WeatherNext 2 (Nov 17 2025) uses a Functional Generative Network to produce hundreds of forecast scenarios in under a minute on one TPU, is 8x faster with up to 1-hour resolution, beats the prior WeatherNext on 99.9% of variables/lead times, and now powers Search, Gemini, Pixel Weather and Maps (data in Earth Engine/BigQuery/Vertex AI).

payload.claim: DeepMind WeatherNext 2 (Nov 2025): FGN model, 8x faster, hundreds of scenarios in <1 min on one TPU, beats prior WeatherNext on 99.9% of variables; shipped to Search/Gemini/Maps.

highlights.title: Periodic Labs — $300M seed for AI-automated materials lab (Fedus + Cubuk)
highlights.detail: Founded by ex-OpenAI post-training lead Liam Fedus and ex-Google Brain materials researcher Ekin Dogus Cubuk (GNoME co-author), Periodic Labs raised a ~$300M seed (a16z lead, Felicis first check; DST, NVentures, Accel; angels Bezos, Schmidt, Gil, Jeff Dean) to pair LLMs, simulation and robotic powder synthesis to discover new materials, starting with superconductors.

payload.name: Periodic Labs
payload.why: Pairs LLMs + simulation + robotic synthesis as an AI-automated materials lab; founded by GNoME co-author Cubuk and ex-OpenAI post-training lead Fedus. One of the most prominent bets that scientific FMs + autonomous labs can discover new materials.
payload.funding: ~$300M seed (Oct 2025), led by a16z (Felicis first check); DST, NVentures, Accel; angels Bezos, Schmidt, Gil, Jeff Dean

highlights.title: Lila Sciences — $200M seed for 'scientific superintelligence' + autonomous labs
highlights.detail: Flagship Pioneering unveiled Lila Sciences (Mar 2025) with a $200M seed to build a scientific-superintelligence platform and autonomous 'AI Science Factories' across life, chemical and materials science (claims include novel green-hydrogen catalysts); investors include General Catalyst, March Capital, ARK and ADIA; chief scientist George Church.

payload.name: Lila Sciences
payload.why: Building scientific-superintelligence + autonomous 'AI Science Factories' spanning materials/chemistry/life science; Flagship-incubated with George Church as chief scientist. A flagship bet on FM-driven autonomous experimentation.
payload.funding: $200M seed (Mar 2025), led by Flagship Pioneering; General Catalyst, March Capital, ARK, ADIA
